protocol_source.note: This criterion's protocol (angle grid + frozen per-angle local_thresholds) was NOT missing -- it is fully specified in the frozen preregistration and is used here verbatim, with no recomputation, no new angle grid, and no multiplier change.

angle_0_role: identity/sanity-check only -- NOT one of the 9 angles counted toward the >=7/9 pass rule (matches the frozen protocol's own list, which includes 0 alongside the 9 non-zero angles, and matches the identical precedent in code_v2/run_synthetic_benchmark.py::measure_equivariance_error, which uses this exact same 10-angle list with angle=0 handled as a no-op)
pass_rule: model_error(angle) < local_threshold(angle) for >= 7 of the 9 non-zero angles

resolutions_of_underspecified_details.item: Input image population for the rotation-consistency test
resolutions_of_underspecified_details.resolution: Pooled testA+testB patches (2083), reused directly from Stage 11's already-established held-out evaluation population (results_v2/baselines/_patch_cache/{testA,testB}.npz) -- NOT a new sample. No patches excluded (including the fragmented testB images). This is a documented reuse of an existing artifact, not an invented population; it also matches the project's established pattern of using the full held-out set for any Stage-11-or-later evaluation.
resolutions_of_underspecified_details.precedent: Same reuse-not-invent resolution pattern as Stage 10's config (configs/stage10_model3_training_config.json).

resolutions_of_underspecified_details.item: Scalar (q1, q2) reduction from Model 3's dense (B, 2, H/2, W/2) output
resolutions_of_underspecified_details.resolution: Center pixel of the dense field ((H/2)//2, (W/2)//2), i.e. same spatial-index convention as oracle_baselines.py::structure_tensor_estimate (which also reduces its dense structure-tensor computation to the single center pixel). This is the SAME reduction convention used to build the frozen real-H&E floor thresholds themselves (via calibration_rotation_floor -> structure_tensor_estimate), so the model-side error is computed compatibly with the floor it is compared against.

resolutions_of_underspecified_details.item: Rotation sign convention for rotating the MODEL's input image
resolutions_of_underspecified_details.resolution: skimage.transform.rotate(img, angle=+alpha_deg, mode='reflect', order=1) -- the MODEL's own verified convention (positive alpha), established independently in code_v2/run_synthetic_benchmark.py::measure_equivariance_error and explicitly NOT the oracle/structure-tensor's convention (which uses angle=-alpha_deg, see code_v2/phase2_calibration.py::calibration_rotation_floor). These two conventions are opposite and must not be conflated -- documented explicitly per project history.
resolutions_of_underspecified_details.precedent: code_v2/run_synthetic_benchmark.py module docstring and measure_equivariance_error function (identical 10-angle list, identical rotate/mode/order arguments, identical normalized_equivariance_error formula).

metric_formula: nematic_math.normalized_equivariance_error: mean_over_patches( ||q_model(R_alpha x) - R(2 alpha).q_model(x)|| / (||R(2 alpha).q_model(x)|| + eps) )
checkpoint: results_v2/model3/checkpoints/checkpoint_final.pt (frozen Stage 10 artifact, MD5 5495ddeba84d3169c2a6b63ad22fbdcb) -- no retraining, no fine-tuning.
additional_checks_from_frozen_file: S(R_alpha x) approx S(x): mean |S_rotated - S_original| across test images and angles
phi(R_alpha x) approx phi(x) + alpha (mod pi): mean angular deviation from expected shift
explicit_scope_limits: This stage measures EMPIRICAL, finite-grid, whole-network rotation consistency under pixel-domain interpolation at specific degree angles -- it does NOT claim mathematically exact continuous equivariance for the complete network.
This stage does NOT alter, rescue, or combine with Stage 11's HOLD status. Stage 11 remains HOLD regardless of this stage's outcome.
No threshold, angle grid, or multiplier is recalculated, tuned, or flattened based on Model 3's observed results.
